Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

United Arab Emirates will be disappointed. They were consistent at the start and got wickets at regular intervals but were sloppy as the game went on. They had a really good chance to keep Scotland near 200. Now, United Arab Emirates have been struggling with the bat. They have lost two games already and a massive task awaits yet again for them. Scotland will be pumped up to defend this. Can United Arab Emirates register their first win? We will find out.

UAE have yet again failed to close the game properly. They have allowed Scotland to get back in the game dearly. Scotland were 48 for 4 at one point and UAE were going along nicely but allowed the middle orders to make an impact. Richie Berrington though glued himself to one end and made some valuable partnerships with the other batters. The skipper got to his century and made sure Scotnald end with more than 250. Watt played a fine camo as well along with Richie Berrington. Scotland will be really pleased with this target.

OUT! RUN OUT! This is full and outside off. Berrington smashes it to covers and calls for a quick couple. Karthik Meiyappan throws it to the keeper who removes the bails. Berrington is short despite the dive. Scotland end with 282.

Hello and welcome to match number 12 in the World Cup Qualifiers where Scotland will take on United Arab Emirates. Two teams who haven't had the best of starts to the tournament will face each other. ...Match Day...

It is now time for match number 12 of the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier, which sees Scotland take on the United Arab Emirates at the Bulawayo Athletic Club. As things stand, Scotland find themselves third in Group B with one win, whereas the United Arab Emirates are languishing at the bottom with two defeats from as many games. Scotland come into this game on the back of a thrilling one-wicket win over Ireland in their opening game of the tournament. In that game, Brandon McMullen starred for them with a five-wicket haul but found little support from the rest of the bowling unit. Moreover, they bowled too many extras and would want to improve on this aspect as they move forward in the competition. With the bat, opener Christopher McBride did provide them with a good start, but the middle-order batters were unable to convert their start into a big one. The likes of Matthew Cross, George Munsey, and Richie Berrington will be expected to step up with the bat this time around. In their pursuit of 287 runs, Scotland were struggling at 152-7, but Michael Leask and Mark Watt got together to put their sides’ innings back on track. Leask remained unbeaten on 91 and saw Scotland home on the penultimate ball of the game. As far as the United Arab Emirates are concerned, they have begun their 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier campaign with back-to-back losses and will be eager to get off the mark. In their last outing against Oman, they were off to a shaky start, losing both openers early. Thanks to knocks by Vriitya Aravind, Rameez Shahzad, and Asif Khan, the United Arab Emirates were able to resurrect the innings a bit. The young left-arm spinner Aayan Khan turned out to be a surprise package with the bat, and he powered his side to a respectable total. A lot will depend on the experienced opening duo of Muhammad Waseem and Rohan Mustafa, who have yet to impress with the bat in the competition. With not a big total to defend, the new ball pair of Junaid Siddique and Ali Naseer began well and did not allow Oman to get off to a flying start. However, the spinners Aayan Khan, Karthik Meiyappan, and Rohan Mustafa were unable to keep the pressure on, and they will be required to be on top of their game against Scotland. In the previous three meetings between the two sides, Scotland emerged victorious on two occasions. Will Scotland continue their dominance over the United Arab Emirates? Or will it be the United Arab Emirates who collect their first points of the tournament? We will find out soon enough.
